intro: Birch Wealthholm arrives with the familiar pitch: AI analysis, automatic entries, a US$300 start and a practice account. The pitch is polished. The fine print is where the questions begin, and that is what this review measures.
It is a web platform with two modes: automatic, where the models execute according to your settings, and manual, where you confirm each entry yourself. Entry costs US$300 and includes a demo.
We do not trade on the platforms we review and we take no referral position in the verdict. We read the pages, verify what is verifiable, and score what remains.
whatItClaims: No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
No platform fees - broker spreads and overnight charges still apply.
Payouts reportedly within a day.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$300, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
US$300, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
The scorecard settles at 4.5. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
